trigger: w10 returned 31/41 as drift, rejecting ::approve idx-edition:<token> turns as grounding. This contradicted w1/w3/w4/w5/w11 who accepted tokenized approvals as qualifying user turns and landed ~300 lines on that basis.
evidence: Supervisor resolved anchors c20260731-194u/116u/193u (w10 drift) and c20260731-79u/60u (w2 drift) via anchory resolve --detail context. In EVERY case the registered v4 line-bound anchor lists the tokenized approval user turns (::approve idx-edition:<token>, ::land-all-approved) as its support members.
ruling: A ::approve idx-edition:<token> user turn IS a qualifying grounding turn for the lines contained in the edition it names. It is the Hugentic capture gate by design - a deliberate, specific accept of a named edition - and Anchory registers it as the line-bound support member. It is categorically different from a bare conversational affirmation of flowing prose.
limit: The token grounds ONLY the lines actually contained in the named edition. A worker must still verify the line was in that edition content. Proximity to a token turn is not grounding.
inconsistency_noted: w10 accepted conversational affirmations (YEEEES, VERY GOOD) while rejecting structured tokenized approvals - backwards relative to the systems own grounding model.
impact: 48 lines on fb3b...ab38 were rejected under the wrong standard: 17 by w2 (rounds 1-2) + 31 by w10. Being requeued for re-inspection under the corrected standard.
